label: The Patriarchs
civContext: Middle Bronze Age Canaan · Egypt's Middle Kingdom
blurb: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob move through Canaan as pastoral clan leaders while Egypt's Middle Kingdom pharaohs rule the Nile and Mesopotamia is a patchwork of city-states.

events.name: Abraham's Call
events.blurb: God calls Abram to leave Ur and Haran for a land he'd only later inherit.

events.name: Jacob Becomes Israel
events.blurb: The covenant passes to Jacob, whose new name becomes the nation's name.

events.name: Joseph in Egypt
events.blurb: Sold into slavery by his brothers, Joseph rises to power in Egypt and saves his family from famine.

label: Bondage & Exodus
civContext: Egypt's New Kingdom — the age of the great empire-building pharaohs
blurb: Jacob's family grows into a nation inside Egypt, is enslaved for generations, and is led out under Moses toward Sinai and, eventually, Canaan.

events.name: Israel Enslaved
events.blurb: A pharaoh who "knew not Joseph" forces the growing Israelite population into hard labor.

events.name: The Exodus
events.blurb: After the plagues, Pharaoh releases Israel, and God parts the Red Sea for their escape.

events.name: The Law at Sinai
events.blurb: God gives Israel the Ten Commandments and the Law at Mount Sinai, formalizing the covenant.

label: Conquest & Judges
civContext: Late Bronze Age collapse · the Philistines (one of the 'Sea Peoples') settle Canaan's coast
blurb: Joshua leads Israel into Canaan; centuries of a repeating cycle — unfaithfulness, oppression, and deliverance — follow under a series of judges, with the Philistines as a recurring rival power.

events.name: Crossing the Jordan
events.blurb: Under Joshua, Israel crosses into Canaan and begins to take the land.

events.name: The Judges Cycle
events.blurb: "Everyone did what was right in his own eyes" — a recurring pattern of drifting, oppression, and rescue.

events.name: Samson & the Philistines
events.blurb: Israel's most famous judge spends his life in conflict with the Philistines on the coastal plain.

label: The United Kingdom
civContext: Phoenician city-states (Tyre, Sidon) flourish as trade partners · Egypt's New Kingdom is fading
blurb: Israel's first kings — Saul, David, and Solomon — unite the twelve tribes into a single kingdom, establish Jerusalem as its capital, and build the Temple.

events.name: Saul, Israel's First King
events.blurb: Israel asks for a king "like all the nations," and Saul is anointed.

events.name: David's Reign
events.blurb: David unites the tribes, takes Jerusalem, and receives God's promise of an everlasting throne.

events.name: Solomon & the Temple
events.blurb: Solomon builds the First Temple in Jerusalem and becomes renowned for wisdom and wealth.

label: Divided Kingdom & the Prophets
civContext: The Neo-Assyrian Empire rises to become the dominant regional power
blurb: After Solomon, the kingdom splits into Israel (north) and Judah (south). Prophets like Elijah, Elisha, Amos, and Hosea confront both nations, until Assyria conquers the northern kingdom.

events.name: The Kingdom Divides
events.blurb: Solomon's son Rehoboam's harshness splits the kingdom into Israel and Judah.

events.name: Elijah & Elisha
events.blurb: Two prophets confront idolatry in the northern kingdom with dramatic signs and miracles.

events.name: The Fall of Israel
events.blurb: Assyria conquers the northern kingdom and deports much of its population.

label: Judah Alone & the Exile
civContext: Assyria dominates, then Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar conquers the entire region
blurb: Judah outlasts Assyria but eventually falls to Babylon; Jerusalem and the Temple are destroyed, and the people are carried into exile — the world of Daniel and Ezekiel.

events.name: Jerusalem Falls
events.blurb: Nebuchadnezzar's Babylonian army destroys Jerusalem and the Temple.

events.name: Daniel in Exile
events.blurb: A young Judean exile rises in Babylon's royal court while staying faithful to God.

events.name: Ezekiel's Visions
events.blurb: From Babylon, Ezekiel sees visions of judgment — and of restoration and new life for Israel.

label: Persian Period & the Return
civContext: Cyrus the Great founds the Persian Achaemenid Empire, the largest the world had yet seen
blurb: Persia conquers Babylon and allows the Jewish exiles to return home. Ezra and Nehemiah rebuild Jerusalem's temple and walls; Esther becomes queen inside the Persian court itself.

events.name: Cyrus's Decree
events.blurb: Cyrus of Persia — named by Isaiah roughly 150 years before he was born — frees the exiles to return.

events.name: Rebuilding Jerusalem
events.blurb: Nehemiah rebuilds Jerusalem's walls in the face of local opposition; Ezra restores the Law.

events.name: Esther in the Persian Court
events.blurb: A Jewish queen in Persia's royal court saves her people from an empire-wide plot.

label: The Greek Age
civContext: Alexander the Great topples Persia and spreads Greek language and culture; after his death, rival Greek kingdoms (the Ptolemies in Egypt, the Seleucids in Syria) fight over Judea
blurb: Roughly four "silent" centuries pass between the Old and New Testaments. Greek becomes the region's common language — setting the stage for the New Testament to be written in Greek — while Daniel had described this very age in advance.

events.name: Daniel's Prophecy of Greece
events.yearLabel: written c. 530s BC, describing events after 332 BC
events.blurb: Daniel's visions describe a swift conquering kingdom — read by many as pointing to Alexander and the four kingdoms that followed his death.

events.name: A Coming Desecration Foreshadowed
events.blurb: A brutal Greek ruler's persecution of Judea — later echoed in Jesus's own end-times teaching.

label: Roman Judea & the Gospels
civContext: Rome annexes Judea as a client territory; Herod the Great and his sons rule under Roman authority; Roman roads and the common Greek language make travel and communication easier than ever before
blurb: Jesus is born under Roman rule during Herod the Great's reign, teaches across Galilee and Judea, and is crucified under the Roman governor Pontius Pilate — then rises again.

events.name: Jesus's Birth Under Rome
events.blurb: A Roman census, a Judean king named Herod, and a child born in Bethlehem.

events.name: Jesus's Ministry
events.blurb: Jesus teaches, heals, and gathers disciples across Galilee and Judea for roughly three years.

events.name: The Crucifixion Under Pilate
events.blurb: Jesus is tried before the Roman governor Pontius Pilate and crucified outside Jerusalem.

label: The Early Church & the Roman Empire
civContext: The gospel spreads along Roman roads and sea routes across the empire — from Jerusalem to Antioch, Asia Minor, Greece, and Rome itself
blurb: The apostles and Paul plant churches across the Roman world. Persecution under emperors like Nero and later Domitian shapes the early church and produces the book of Revelation.

events.name: Pentecost & the Church's Birth
events.blurb: The Holy Spirit comes on the disciples in Jerusalem, and the church begins.

events.name: Paul's Journeys Across the Empire
events.blurb: Paul plants churches from Antioch to Asia Minor to Greece, then reaches Rome itself.

events.name: Revelation Under Roman Persecution
events.blurb: Exiled on Patmos under Emperor Domitian, John writes to churches enduring pressure to compromise or suffer.
